## Feature

```python
# In CPython
>>> type(dict.__dict__["fromkeys"])
<class 'classmethod_descriptor'>
>>> type(dict.fromkeys)
<class 'builtin_function_or_method'>

# In RustPython
>>>>> type(dict.__dict__["fromkeys"])
<class 'classmethod'>
>>>>> type(dict.fromkeys)
<class 'builtin_function_or_method'>
```

- `<class 'classmethod'>` is for descriptors of Python-side `@classmethod`.
  - `PyClassMethod_Type` in CPython
  - `PyClassMethod` in RustPython
- `<class 'classmethod_descriptor'>` is for descriptors of **native-side** class method.
  - `PyClassMethodDescr_Type` in CPython
  - Nothing in RustPython, instead using `PyClassMethod`

(Yeah, these names are somewhat confusing...)

In short, RustPython uses a different type from CPython for built-in class methods.

I don't know if it causes any real difference in behavior. There is no test for this in CPython (only [a mysterious comment](https://github.com/python/cpython/blob/0c857865e4f255f99d58678f878e09c11da89892/Lib/test/test_sys.py#L1383) exists)
